title: Finite type algebra with finite spectrum is finite-dimensional
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $B$ be a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. If $\operatorname{Spec} B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has finitely many prime ideals, then every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal, $B$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space, and $\operatorname{Spec} B$ is a finite discrete space. The zero ring is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 00KH (Noetherian dimension 0) together with Lemma 0ALW (finite type algebra with finitely many prime ideals)

proof.text: The algebra B is Jacobson by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal], implemented by isJacobsonRing_of_finiteType with base k. PrimeSpectrum.instJacobsonSpace makes its prime spectrum a Jacobson space. Since this spectrum is finite, Mathlib's finite-Jacobson-space DiscreteTopology instance gives discrete Zariski topology. Concretely, closed points are dense in a Jacobson space; they form a finite closed set here, so they exhaust the space. Every subset is then a finite union of closed points and hence closed.

Every singleton in the discrete spectrum is closed. By PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal, each prime ideal is maximal. PrimeSpectrum.discreteTopology_iff_finite_and_krullDimLE_zero also gives Ring.KrullDimLE 0 B.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-dim-zero-finite], implemented by Module.finite_iff_krullDimLE_zero over the Artinian field k, to the dimension bound just obtained. This gives Module.Finite k B. Combine maximality, finiteness as a module, and discreteness. The proof requires no Nontrivial B hypothesis, and covers the zero ring, whose spectrum is empty.
